newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARCELONA SAY RONALDO WILL STAY WITH TEAM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA SAY RONALDO WILL STAY WITH TEAM.

text.p: Brazilian striker Ronaldo has renewed a 10-year contract with Spanish soccer club Barcelona, a club spokesman told Reuters on Tuesday.

The 20-year-old striker signed on for nine more years at 500 million pesetas ($3.5 million) a season with the Catalan club after protracted talks on the cost of breaking his contract, which was finally set at 10 billion pesetas ($69.9 million).

Barcelona had been holding out for 15 billion pesetas ($104.85 million), almost double the amount clubs have to pay to poach other star players from Spain and almost treble the four billion ($27.98 million) set when Ronaldo first signed the contract in 1996.

Italian, English and French clubs had shown interest in the striker, who with 34 goals has scored far more this season than any other player in the Spanish championship league or even the European league's Golden Boot competition.
Ronaldo was in Oslo on Tuesday playing for his national team..

Barcelona president Jose Luis Nunez told a news conference that Ronaldo had "made good on his word" and had held to the agreed financial terms signed in December even though the deal had expired and he had received big offers from other clubs.
Ronaldo's agents said that an overriding issue for the young player was his desire to remain with Barcelona, where he had made good friends and enjoyed the lifestyle in Catalonia.

But his agent, Giovanni Branchini, told journalists the nine hours of negotiations on Monday and Tuesday had "not been easy" and Ronaldo had been prepared to go to Inter Milan if a deal had not been possible.
